<div id="bx-article">

  <div class="bx-pills">
    <span class="bx-pill">Development</span>
    <span class="bx-pill">PHP</span>
    <span class="bx-pill">PDF</span>
    <span class="bx-pill">Reporting</span>
  </div>

  <p class="bx-lede">A report that only lives on screen is easy to lose track of. Generating PDF reports in PHP turns that data into one downloadable file a client, a manager, or an accounting system can actually keep.</p>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">01</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="generating-pdf-reports-in-php-starts-with-picking-the-right-tool">Generating PDF Reports in PHP Starts With Picking the Right Tool</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>There are two common families of tools for this job. A Composer installed library such as <a href="https://dompdf.github.io/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Dompdf</a>, <a href="https://tcpdf.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">TCPDF</a>, or <a href="https://mpdf.github.io/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">mPDF</a> renders markup directly inside the PHP process itself.</p>

  <p>The other route shells out to a separate rendering engine that takes a full page of real HTML and CSS and turns it into a PDF outside PHP entirely, the approach this article builds around.</p>

  <p>Both routes produce a real file that follows the same underlying <a href="https://www.iso.org/standard/75839.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">ISO 32000 PDF specification</a>, so the difference is really about where the rendering happens and what dependencies the hosting environment allows.</p>

  <div class="bx-table-wrap">
    <table class="bx-table">
      <thead>
        <tr style="background:#2b2b2b !important;">
          <th style="background:#2b2b2b !important; color:#ffffff !important;">Approach</th>
          <th style="background:#2b2b2b !important; color:#ffffff !important;">How It Renders</th>
          <th style="background:#2b2b2b !important; color:#ffffff !important;">Best Fit</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Composer library (Dompdf, TCPDF, mPDF)</td><td>Builds the PDF inside the PHP process directly</td><td>Simple layouts, shared hosting without shell access</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Shell out to wkhtmltopdf</td><td>A separate rendering engine converts a real HTML page</td><td>Complex CSS layouts, an existing HTML template</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Hosted PDF rendering API</td><td>The HTML is sent to a remote rendering service</td><td>No local binary or library to maintain at all</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <div class="bx-ad">
    <script async src="https://pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js?client=ca-pub-3931314195561246" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
    <ins class="adsbygoogle" style="display:block" data-ad-client="ca-pub-3931314195561246" data-ad-slot="4249015278" data-ad-format="auto" data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>
    <script>(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});</script>
  </div>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">02</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="building-the-report-template-and-the-data-behind-it">Building the Report Template and the Data Behind It</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>A PDF report is only as good as the HTML it starts from. Keeping the template as a separate function from the data that fills it makes the same layout reusable for an invoice, a monthly summary, or any other report the site needs.</p>

  <p>The line items below could just as easily come from a database, pulled with the same kind of prepared statement covered in <a href="/php-pdo-prepared-statements/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">PHP PDO prepared statements</a>, rather than the fixed array used here for a clear demonstration.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">generate_invoice.php</div>
    <pre><code><span class="tok-kw">function</span> <span class="tok-fn">render_invoice_html</span>(<span class="tok-kw">array</span> <span class="tok-val">$invoice</span>): <span class="tok-kw">string</span>
{
    <span class="tok-val">$rowsHtml</span> = <span class="tok-str">''</span>;
    <span class="tok-val">$total</span> = <span class="tok-val">0</span>;

    <span class="tok-kw">foreach</span> (<span class="tok-val">$invoice</span>[<span class="tok-str">'items'</span>] <span class="tok-kw">as</span> <span class="tok-val">$item</span>) {
        <span class="tok-val">$lineTotal</span> = <span class="tok-val">$item</span>[<span class="tok-str">'qty'</span>] * <span class="tok-val">$item</span>[<span class="tok-str">'price'</span>];
        <span class="tok-val">$total</span> += <span class="tok-val">$lineTotal</span>;
        <span class="tok-val">$rowsHtml</span> .= sprintf(
            <span class="tok-str">'&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;%s&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;%d&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;$%.2f&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;$%.2f&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;'</span>,
            htmlspecialchars(<span class="tok-val">$item</span>[<span class="tok-str">'name'</span>]),
            <span class="tok-val">$item</span>[<span class="tok-str">'qty'</span>],
            <span class="tok-val">$item</span>[<span class="tok-str">'price'</span>],
            <span class="tok-val">$lineTotal</span>
        );
    }

    <span class="tok-kw">return</span> <span class="tok-str">"&lt;html&gt;...&lt;/html&gt;"</span>; <span class="tok-cm">// full HTML template with the rows above inserted</span>
}</code></pre>
  </div>

  <div class="bx-tip">
    <span class="bx-tip-label">Tip</span>
    <p>Run every dynamic value through <code>htmlspecialchars()</code> before it lands in the template, the same rule covered in <a href="/validating-and-sanitizing-user-input-in-php-forms/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">validating and sanitizing user input in PHP forms</a>. A report is still an HTML page until it gets converted, and it can still carry an injection risk if a customer name is left unescaped.</p>
  </div>

  <p>Keeping styling inline or in a single embedded stylesheet matters here too, since the rendering engine converting the page has no access to the site's own external CSS files once the HTML is handed off.</p>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">03</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="converting-the-template-into-a-real-pdf-file">Converting the Template Into a Real PDF File</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>Once the HTML template is saved to a real file, the actual conversion step is a single shell command. <a href="https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.system.php" target="_blank" rel="noopener">PHP's system() function</a> hands that command off to the operating system and captures its exit code.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">generate_invoice.php</div>
    <pre><code><span class="tok-val">$html</span> = <span class="tok-fn">render_invoice_html</span>(<span class="tok-val">$invoice</span>);
file_put_contents(__DIR__ . <span class="tok-str">'/invoice.html'</span>, <span class="tok-val">$html</span>);

<span class="tok-val">$exitCode</span> = <span class="tok-kw">null</span>;
system(<span class="tok-str">'wkhtmltopdf --quiet '</span> . __DIR__ . <span class="tok-str">'/invoice.html '</span> . __DIR__ . <span class="tok-str">'/invoice.pdf'</span>, <span class="tok-val">$exitCode</span>);

echo <span class="tok-str">"wkhtmltopdf exit code: $exitCode\n"</span>;</code></pre>
  </div>

  <p>Running that exact script for real against the invoice template above, then checking the file it produced with <code>pdfinfo</code>, gives an honest look at what actually happened rather than an assumption that it worked.</p>

  <div class="bx-shot">
    <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="Real terminal output showing wkhtmltopdf exit code 0, invoice.pdf created successfully, and pdfinfo confirming a valid one page A4 PDF file" />
  </div>
  <p class="bx-shot-caption">Actual terminal output from running the script above and checking the result with pdfinfo.</p>

  <div class="bx-fact">
    <span class="bx-fact-label">Did You Know</span>
    <p>The wkhtmltopdf project itself has been described by its own maintainers as <a href="https://github.com/KnpLabs/snappy/issues/529" target="_blank" rel="noopener">deprecated since 2023</a>, with no active development continuing since. It still runs and produces valid files, but it is worth planning a migration path toward a maintained alternative for any long running production project.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">04</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="verifying-the-pdf-that-was-actually-produced">Verifying the PDF That Was Actually Produced</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>A successful exit code is a good sign, but it is not proof the file is a real, readable PDF. Checking <code>file_exists()</code> alone would pass even for an empty, zero byte file.</p>

  <p>A more reliable check reads the first few bytes of the file and confirms they match the <code>%PDF</code> signature every valid PDF file starts with, or shells out to a tool built specifically for that job.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">verify_pdf.php</div>
    <pre><code><span class="tok-val">$handle</span> = fopen(<span class="tok-val">$pdfPath</span>, <span class="tok-str">'rb'</span>);
<span class="tok-val">$header</span> = fread(<span class="tok-val">$handle</span>, <span class="tok-val">5</span>);
fclose(<span class="tok-val">$handle</span>);

<span class="tok-val">$isRealPdf</span> = str_starts_with(<span class="tok-val">$header</span>, <span class="tok-str">'%PDF-'</span>);</code></pre>
  </div>

  <p>The <a href="https://www.freedesktop.org/wiki/Software/poppler/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Poppler project's</a> <code>pdfinfo</code> and <code>pdftoppm</code> command line tools go a step further, actually parsing the file's internal structure and reporting page count, page size, and PDF version, or rendering a page to an image so a human can look at the real result.</p>

  <div class="bx-shot">
    <img src="data:image/png;base64," alt="The actual first page of the generated PDF invoice, rendered from the real PDF file with pdftoppm, showing the invoice number, customer name, itemized table, and total" />
  </div>
  <p class="bx-shot-caption">The real first page of invoice.pdf, rendered straight from the actual generated file rather than a mockup.</p>

  <div class="bx-tip">
    <span class="bx-tip-label">Tip</span>
    <p>Rendering a page with <code>pdftoppm</code> during automated testing catches layout problems, like a table overflowing the page width, that a passing exit code and a valid file signature would both miss entirely.</p>
  </div>

    <script async src="https://pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js?client=ca-pub-3931314195561246" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
    <ins class="adsbygoogle" style="display:block" data-ad-client="ca-pub-3931314195561246" data-ad-slot="4249015278" data-ad-format="auto" data-full-width-responsive="true"></ins>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">05</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="storing-and-serving-generated-pdf-reports-securely">Storing and Serving Generated PDF Reports Securely</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>A generated report file deserves the same caution as any user uploaded file. It should sit outside the public web root, under a random name, following the same reasoning covered in <a href="/php-file-upload-security/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">PHP file upload security</a>.</p>

  <p>Serving the file back to a browser then means reading it through a small PHP script that checks the current user actually owns that report, instead of exposing a direct, guessable file path.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">download_report.php</div>
    <pre><code>header(<span class="tok-str">'Content-Type: application/pdf'</span>);
header(<span class="tok-str">'Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="invoice-'</span> . <span class="tok-val">$invoiceNumber</span> . <span class="tok-str">'.pdf"'</span>);
header(<span class="tok-str">'Content-Length: '</span> . filesize(<span class="tok-val">$pdfPath</span>));
readfile(<span class="tok-val">$pdfPath</span>);</code></pre>
  </div>

  <p>The <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Disposition" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Content-Disposition header reference on MDN</a> covers the difference between <code>attachment</code>, which forces a download, and <code>inline</code>, which opens the PDF directly in the browser tab instead.</p>

  <p>The <a href="https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">OWASP file handling guidance</a> applies just as much to files a server generates as to files a user uploads, particularly around never trusting a client supplied path when reading a file back off disk.</p>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">06</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="scheduling-pdf-reports-to-generate-on-their-own">Scheduling PDF Reports to Generate on Their Own</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>Plenty of reports do not need a person to click a button at all. A nightly sales summary or a weekly export reads more naturally as a scheduled job than as something someone has to remember to run.</p>

  <p>The overlap locking and structured logging pattern covered in <a href="/php-cron-jobs/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">PHP cron jobs</a> applies directly here too, since a report generation script that runs twice at once can produce a half written file.</p>

  <div class="bx-code-wrap">
    <div class="bx-code-title">crontab</div>
    <pre><code><span class="tok-cm"># runs every night at 2am, generates the previous day's report</span>
0 2 * * * php /var/www/scripts/generate_daily_report.php >> /var/log/pdf_reports.log 2>&1</code></pre>
  </div>

  <div class="bx-section-head">
    <span class="bx-num">07</span>
    <h2 class="bx-h2" id="choosing-between-wkhtmltopdf-and-a-composer-library-in-production">Choosing Between wkhtmltopdf and a Composer Library in Production</h2>
    <div class="bx-rule"></div>
  </div>

  <p>The right choice usually comes down to what the hosting environment actually allows, and how complex the report layout needs to be.</p>

  <ul class="bx-checklist">
    <li><b>Shell access is required for wkhtmltopdf:</b> shared hosting without <code>system()</code> or <code>exec()</code> access rules this option out entirely.</li>
    <li><b>Composer libraries work anywhere PHP runs:</b> Dompdf, TCPDF, and mPDF need no shell access, only a Composer install.</li>
    <li><b>Complex CSS renders more accurately through wkhtmltopdf:</b> it uses a real browser style engine rather than each library's own partial CSS support.</li>
    <li><b>Always verify the output file, not just the exit code:</b> a real file check catches failures a passing status code alone would miss.</li>
    <li><b>Plan for wkhtmltopdf's unmaintained status:</b> it still works today, but a long running project should track a maintained alternative.</li>
  </ul>

  <div class="bx-faq">
    <h3 class="bx-h3">Frequently Asked Questions</h3>

    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">1</span><span>What is the easiest way of generating PDF reports in PHP?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>Shelling out to a preinstalled binary like wkhtmltopdf with system() is often the fastest path when shell access is available, since it renders real HTML and CSS without needing a Composer library at all.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">2</span><span>Does generating PDF reports in PHP require Composer?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>No. Composer is only needed for library based options like Dompdf, TCPDF, or mPDF. Shelling out to a system binary skips Composer entirely.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">3</span><span>Is wkhtmltopdf still safe to use in production?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>It still runs and produces valid files today, but the project itself has been described as deprecated since 2023 with no active development, so a long running project should plan for an eventual migration.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">4</span><span>How can a generated PDF be verified as actually valid?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>Check the file's first bytes for the %PDF signature, or use a tool like pdfinfo, rather than trusting a passing exit code or file_exists() alone.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="bx-faq-item">
      <button type="button" class="bx-faq-q"><span class="bx-faq-num">5</span><span>Can generating PDF reports in PHP happen automatically on a schedule?</span></button>
      <div class="bx-faq-a"><p>Yes, a cron job can run the same generation script nightly or weekly, with overlap locking to prevent two runs writing to the same file at once.</p></div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="bx-learn">
    <h2 id="what-we-learn-today">What We Learn Today</h2>
    <div class="bx-learn-grid">
      <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">1</span><div><h4>Two real paths for PDF generation</h4><p>Shell out to a renderer, or use a Composer library.</p></div></div>
      <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">2</span><div><h4>wkhtmltopdf uses a real render engine</h4><p>Full HTML and CSS convert more accurately than partial support.</p></div></div>

      <div class="bx-learn-card"><span class="bx-learn-num">4</span><div><h4>Serve reports through a script</h4><p>Never a raw, guessable public file path.</p></div></div>

<script>
(function() {
  var items = document.querySelectorAll('.bx-faq-item');

  items.forEach(function(item) {
    var q = item.querySelector('.bx-faq-q');
    var a = item.querySelector('.bx-faq-a');

    item.classList.add('open');
    a.style.maxHeight = a.scrollHeight + 'px';

    q.addEventListener('click', function() {
      var isOpen = item.classList.contains('open');
      if (isOpen) {
        item.classList.remove('open');
        a.style.maxHeight = null;
      } else {
        item.classList.add('open');
        a.style.maxHeight = a.scrollHeight + 'px';
      }
    });
  });
})();
</script>
